items.title: Frank Foster — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: The interviewee acknowledges the name 'Chick Webb' but the subsequent speech is a monologue about Frank Wess and the flute, with no mention of any personal interaction, collaboration, or specific relationship with Chick Webb.

ctx.x: Chick Webb, okay. There were a great number of years in which the flute was not heard of after Carver’s presentation of it. Frank Wess reintroduced it, and it became a very, very popular instrument, as you all know. He was very proficient on the flute. He wasn’t just -- it wasn’t something he just picked up and started playing. He had been working on the flute. He was an excellent flautist, so he had that dimension going for him. My extra dimension was my composing and arranging. In that area I contributed widely…

I just want to ask one more thing about the two tenor thing. How did Basie orchestrate an evening by sequencing things? What role did those certain features, where maybe there might be -- the two tenor thing might be happening -- where did that fit in?
